transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ko (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Bluebloom Product Lead), Marcus Hale (Head of ML), Priya Singh (SRE)

Auto-summary (generated): Weekly POC fidelity check; flagged regression on intent extraction after prompt tweak; guardrail tightening increased false positives in support flows; agreed to bisection + targeted benchmark and to share security docs.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, quick check — can you all hear me?
[00:03] Lena: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:06] Marcus: Good here.
[00:08] Samira: Great. This is the weekly standup for the POC — fidelity and guardrail work. We have about 40 minutes. Ethan's gonna lead through the failing cases and then we'll go over next steps.
[00:20] Ethan: Cool. So I pulled the latest scorecard — we ran your 5k test set last night after the prompt edit. Overall intent accuracy dropped 3.4 points, hallucination rate up about 1.9%. The interesting part is the distribution: most of the regressions are in the "extract payment details" intent and the support-cancellation flow.
[00:40] Lena: Mm-hmm. Right after we tightened the guardrail for PIIs, we started seeing more incomplete extractions. Is that what you mean?
[00:48] Ethan: Exactly. When we increased the safety threshold and added stricter entity masks, the model is being over-conservative — returning NULL or refusing. So false negatives went up.
[00:58] Marcus: Do you have examples? I want to see what the model is masking as PII incorrectly.
[01:02] Ethan: Yeah, I prepared a short list. I'll share — Link: https://redwood.ai/poc/bluebloom/partials.csv (note: internal link). Example 27 — user says "last four of card 1234" and the model returns refusal. That used to be tolerated as non-sensitive in your policy but with stricter KG the mask hits.
[01:24] Lena: Ugh, okay. That's the customer experience regression we feared. Some of those flows are high volume.
[01:28] Samira: Quick clarifying Q — Marcus, is explicit PCI masking required at inference, or can we do post-processing on parameterized results?
[01:36] Marcus: Ideally post-process, but compliance team is nervous. Priya, do you have the SRE take?
[01:40] Priya: From infra POV we'd prefer post-process too — avoids overfitting prompts to safety policies — but the audit trail needs to show we never logged raw card numbers. KMS to encrypt outputs, S O C two audit requirement — is that S O C two, sorry.
[01:55] Samira: Yeah SOC 2. We'll include our SOC 2 and encryption docs in the handoff.
[01:59] Marcus: Cool.
[02:02] Ethan: Back to regressions — I ran a quick A/B across model variants we have onboarded in your POC: base-7b-qat, base-13b-fp16, and a 13b-int8 variant. The 13b-fp16 does best on extraction while the int8 variant is slightly cheaper but shows more hallucination under long context. Latency at your 256-token average is 120ms for 13b-fp16 on Dedicated, 160ms for int8 on Hosted.
[02:32] Lena: 120ms is fine, but cost is going to be discussed — what's the per-token delta?
[02:36] Ethan: Rough numbers: about 20% higher per-token for the fp16 13b vs int8. But because of fewer retries and lower post-processing, effective cost per successful extraction may be parity or even lower.
[02:50] Marcus: Interesting, so better model reduces downstream cost. We need the calculation though.
[02:55] Samira: We'll attach a cost-breakdown spreadsheet. I'll include both per-token and effective per-successful-extraction numbers.
[03:02] Lena: Thanks. On the guardrails, I noticed tightening made support bot refuse on non-sensitive items — like "order #". Is that in the same mask rules?
[03:12] Ethan: Yeah, some token patterns like "order #" are triggering heuristics. There's a balance — you don't want to leak PII, but we can tune by whitelisting certain schemas like internal order IDs that are non-PII.
[03:26] Priya: Are whitelist rules manageable from our side? We need RBAC so only product/security can edit them.
[03:32] Samira: Yes, the console supports rule sets with role-based access; we'll show that in the demo next week.
[03:37] Lena: Great.
[03:39] Ethan: For the regression hunt I propose a bisection: we take the 120 failing cases flagged, split into semantic buckets (payment, cancellation, support), then run targeted prompt rewrites for each bucket and measure deltas. If a rewrite reduces false negatives without bumping hallucination, we push.
[03:58] Marcus: Sounds good. What's the time estimate?
[04:00] Ethan: For an initial pass — 2 dev-days. I can get the narrowed seed set to you in 48 hours.
[04:06] Marcus: Okay.
[04:08] Samira: Ethan, can you also try restoring the previous guardrail threshold as a quick A/B to confirm the regression is strictly from the safety change?
[04:15] Ethan: Yep, I already queued that — that'll be part of the bisection.
[04:18] Lena: On scoring, a note — some of our business rules mark a partial extraction as acceptable if confidence > 0.8. Can we integrate model confidence into the scorecard?
[04:27] Ethan: We can. We'll add confidence and also per-field confidence for extraction tasks. That will help you choose post-process paths.
[04:34] Samira: I'll update the scorecard template to include per-field confidence and a suggested post-process flow.
[04:39] Lena: Perfect.
[04:41] Marcus: Security checkpoint — can you confirm we can run the benchmark in our VPC? We prefer not to route any raw user traffic through hosted endpoints.
[04:50] Samira: Yes, Dedicated or Private deployment supports VPC peering or our private control plane. For the POC we can do a short dedicated burst with egress controls. Pricing varies but I'll send options.
[05:01] Priya: Also KMS integration — we need to ensure customer-managed keys; can Redwood integrate with AWS KMS/HSM?
[05:08] Ethan: Yes, we support customer-managed keys on Dedicated and Private. There's an integration doc I'll share. Note: certain automatic caching behaviors require additional config when using CMKs.
[05:20] Lena: Which caching behaviors?
[05:22] Ethan: Prefix/KV cache — how we store KV cache for recurring contexts. When encryption is enforced at rest with CMK, the cache needs to be handled differently; that can slightly affect latency.
[05:33] Marcus: I think that's acceptable if we have the confidentiality guarantee.
[05:36] Samira: We'll include the KMS/KV cache tradeoffs in the doc.
[05:40] Lena: Awesome.
[05:42] Ethan: Moving to false positives — after the tighten we saw a +6% refusal rate across help center intents. Many are borderline; I recommend two mitigations: relax mask on known-safe schemas and add a small post-classifier to re-check refusals for high-value flows.
[05:59] Marcus: Can that classifier be hosted on our infra? We want control.
[06:03] Ethan: Yes — you can run a lightweight binary in your infra that takes the model output and applies a second-level policy. Redwood also offers an optional re-check hook.
[06:12] Priya: That might be our preference. We'll run the re-check in our VPC and only call Redwood for final gen.
[06:18] Samira: Good plan.
[06:20] Lena: Now, on the evaluation rubric — I noticed the thresholds are a bit tight for support flows. Can we adjust the scoring weights so extraction recall has higher weight for support and hallucination has higher weight for payments?
[06:33] Ethan: Absolutely. The scorecard is config-driven per-route. We'll add a support-route profile with recall-weight 0.6 and halluc-weight 0.4, and a payments profile inverse.
[06:45] Marcus: Nice.
[06:47] Ethan: For the regression tracking, I'll push an annotated heatmap to the shared folder showing per-example diffs. That should help triage.
[06:56] Lena: Thanks — that will help product prioritize.
[06:59] Samira: Quick check on benchmarks — Marcus, can you give us the shape of the synthetic workload? You mentioned 1k queries?
[07:06] Marcus: Yeah, 1k queries that replicate the top-10 user utterances and a long-tail 4k sample; for cost run we'll start with the 1k to keep it quick. Latency target is p95 < 300ms.
[07:18] Ethan: On Dedicated with 13b-fp16 we see p95 ~ 180ms at your expected QPS for a single shard. If you need sustained throughput, we can recommend reserve capacity.
[07:29] Samira: I'll include a Dedicated commitment option that maps to QPS ranges.
[07:33] Priya: One thing — do you have any concerns around model caching and multitenancy noise with our traffic in a shared environment?
[07:40] Ethan: On Hosted, there can be cache warm/cold effects; Dedicated gives you isolated pools so KV cache is private and predictable. For this POC if predictability matters, Dedicated for benchmark is better.
[07:52] Lena: Understood. We'll take your Dedicated option seriously for the benchmark run.
[07:56] Samira: Anything else on compliance? Marcus?
[07:58] Marcus: We'll want your SOC 2 and data retention policy. Also SLA around data deletion.
[08:04] Samira: Got it. I'll attach SOC 2 summary, retention policy, and a one-pager on deletion APIs.
[08:10] Lena: Cool.
[08:12] Ethan: Final technical note — one of the failing cases looks like a tokenization split causing entity mismatch. That's on the tokenizer rules. For that we can add normalization in pre-process. I'll include a patch.
[08:24] Lena: Thank you.
[08:25] Samira: Ok let's recap next steps quickly. Ethan will run bisection and share failing buckets in 48 hours. Samira will update and share the prompt set + scorecard + pricing and security docs. Marcus will upload the 1k synthetic queries. Priya will send SSO/KMS questions.
[08:44] Marcus: Yep.
[08:45] Priya: Yep.
[08:46] Samira: Great. We'll schedule the infra deep dive for next week — I'll send a calendar invite with a couple of slots.
[08:52] Lena: Thanks everyone.
[08:54] Ethan: Thanks, bye.
[08:55] Samira: Bye.

--- End transcript ---
